title: Manifest V2: publish performance profiles and explicit version-binding semantics
creator: Maya Chen
description: Add a Manifest V2 object to the model catalog API that (1) publishes per-model performance profiles (latency percentiles, token throughput at common batch sizes, observed memcpy/IO cost behavior), (2) surfaces capability flags (streaming, function-calling, embeddings-only, kv-cache-friendly), and (3) defines explicit version-binding semantics to support deterministic pinning and graceful fallbacks. This ticket covers schema design, runtime mapping rules, SDK surface changes, docs, and a staged rollout with backward compatibility for clients relying on Manifest V1.
motivation: Customers require stable, discoverable performance characteristics for model selection and price/latency trade-offs. Current minimal 'capabilities' surface doesn't encode performance buckets or pinning semantics, forcing apps to run expensive live benchmarks or hard-pin undocumented variants. Manifest V2 lets us advertise tested profiles and an explicit 'binding' contract so Hosted, Dedicated and Private deployments can behave consistently.
goals: Define Manifest V2 JSON schema and server-side validation
Introduce version_binding enum: exact | semver_major | compatible | floating
Publish performance profiles including context_window, baseline_99_latency_ms, tokens_per_sec_at_batch_1, tokens_per_sec_at_batch_8
Add capability flags: streaming, function_calling, structured_output, kv_cache_friendly, quantized_supported
Maintain Manifest V1 for 6 months and provide clear migration docs and feature gates
SDK changes: add Model.manifest_v2 accessor and pinning helpers in python/js sdks
Add CI checks validating model manifest_v2 when new models are onboarded
acceptance_criteria: API returns manifest_v2 for existing test models without breaking existing clients when manifest_version header absent
Requesting manifest_version=2 returns the new schema with performance_profiles array and binding semantics
Runtime routing honors version_binding rules in unit/integration tests (exact and semver_major paths covered)
Docs updated with examples for pinning strategies and fallback behaviors
SDK patch released with model.manifest_v2 accessor and tests
Migration guide published and signals enabled in console to show models missing manifest_v2
api_changes: Add GET /v1/models/:id?manifest_version=2 to return ManifestV2 (default remains V1)
ManifestV2 top-level fields: model_id, variant, version, version_binding, performance_profiles, capability_flags, recommended_batching, recommended_quantization, deprecation_date
performance_profiles is an ordered array of named profiles: {name, max_context_tokens, median_latency_ms, p99_latency_ms, tokens_per_sec_at_batch_1, tokens_per_sec_at_8, cost_multiplier}
capability_flags is a list of strings: streaming, function_calling, structured_output, embeddings, kv_cache_friendly, hf_compat
Clients may pass header X-Model-Binding: exact|semver_major|compatible to request intended binding enforcement behavior for allocation planning (server ignores if not supported)
POST /v1/models/:id/manifest_v2 for internal onboarding pipeline with server validation and signature check
implementation_notes: Server: add manifest_v2 marshaller and validator in model-catalog service; reuse existing model storage but store manifest_v2 as signed artifact
Runtime: map performance_profiles to scheduler hints: preferred_batch_size, prefetch_kv_cache, kernel_selection_hint
Routing: when a request includes explicit pin (model:version), enforce exact; when pinning uses semantic rules, translate to compatible variant list using manifest_v2.rules
Onboarding: update ingest pipeline to run bench harness on canonical machines and produce p50/p99 and throughput numbers as part of manifest_v2
Backward compatibility: default endpoints return V1 unless client opts-in to V2; build a feature flag to flip default for internal customers
Observability: emit manifest_v2.version and profile.name in trace/span tags and console dashboards for per-profile latency breakdowns
rollout_plan: Onboarding pipeline changes & bench harness - week 2-3
Runtime mapping and routing tests - week 3-4
Internal dogfood: expose V2 to Redwood internal clients behind flag - week 5
Gradual public rollout: opt-in then switch default after 6 weeks with deprecation warnings - week 6-12
test_plan: Unit tests for manifest_v2 validator and schema diffs
Integration tests: routing honors version_binding for exact and semver_major
Bench regression tests to ensure published p99 numbers are within 10% of observed on CI hardware
E2E tests with SDK pinning helpers that simulate fallback behavior when a variant is unavailable
Security tests: signature verification for manifest artifacts and role-based access for POST /manifest_v2
migration_steps: 1) Publish Manifest V2 for all newly onboarded models going forward
2) Backfill key production models with v2 over 8 weeks prioritized by usage
3) Expose console signal and alerts for models lacking recommended_batching or p99 fields
4) After 6 months, change default served manifest_version to 2 with a public deprecation notice for V1
5) Final removal of V1 after 12 months with clear customer communications and tooling to convert client pinning
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: clients relying on current undocumented behavior may break if server starts enforcing pinning rules. Mitigation: opt-in flag + long migration window.
Risk: published perf numbers differ from private customer hardware. Mitigation: include compute-hint metadata and expected hardware SKU used for benchmarking.
Risk: manifest artifacts could be tampered. Mitigation: sign manifests and validate signature server-side; require ACL for POSTs.
notes: This ticket intentionally separates semantics from presentation: ManifestV2 is canonical for programmatic routing and cost/latency decisions. UX-focused presentation work for Console will be tracked in a follow-up PM ticket. Coordinate with product-design and infra for KMS access for manifest signing.
